evidence.observation: get_parser() constructs the configargparse.ArgumentParser with add_config_file_help=True, default_config_files=default_config_files, config_file_parser_class=configargparse.YAMLConfigFileParser and auto_env_var_prefix="AIDER_". This is what gives every option declared inside get_parser three non-CLI input sources: the AIDER_<OPT> environment variable, the .aider.conf.yml config file, and the add_argument default. It is the env/config half of the precedence contract that explicit CLI input has to beat.

The T07 fixture option is declared here as group.add_argument("--suggest-shell-commands", action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction, default=True, help=...). BooleanOptionalAction registers both the positive and the negative CLI spelling against the same dest suggest_shell_commands, so an explicit CLI occurrence of either polarity is expressible; default=True means an override is observable as False rather than being indistinguishable from 'unset'. Combined with the AIDER_ prefix, the env source is AIDER_SUGGEST_SHELL_COMMANDS.

The tri-state member of the same declaration family: --analytics is also action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction but with default=None, so its domain is the three values None (unset/random), True and False. The C-T07 precedence rule reads identically here; only the 'no input' value differs, which is why the project probe asserts [] -> None, --analytics -> True, --no-analytics -> False.

The unrelated-default control option: an independent boolean declaration (action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction, default=True) in the 'Other settings' group with no derivation from --suggest-shell-commands. The contract requires its value to stay True while --suggest-shell-commands is overridden, which is what the probe's controls-unchanged and cli control rows check. --cache-prompts (aider/args.py:232-237, default=False) is the second control.

Part of the repository's existing acceptance fixture for the T07 option: test_suggest_shell_commands_default (735-743), _disabled (745-753) and _enabled (755-763) each call main([...], return_coder=True) inside GitTemporaryDirectory() and assert coder.suggest_shell_commands is exactly True/False/True. This establishes the *observable* that T07 speaks about (the coder attribute, not merely the parsed namespace) and the trio covers CLI-versus-default; T07 extends it with the env/config-versus-CLI opposition that the trio does not test.

Shows that environment input is genuinely consumed by the same parser and wired into behavior: an .env file containing AIDER_DARK_MODE=True passed via --env-file makes main() build InputOutput with code_theme="monokai". Together with test_default_env_file_sets_automatic_variable (436-446), test_false_vals_in_env_file (448-454, AIDER_SHOW_DIFFS=off -> show_diffs False) and test_true_vals_in_env_file (456-462, AIDER_SHOW_DIFFS=on -> True), this proves the env source is real and boolean-valued -- i.e. there is a non-default value for an explicit CLI flag to override.

The harness that makes the fixture reproducible: it snapshots os.environ, forces OPENAI_API_KEY, AIDER_CHECK_UPDATE=false and AIDER_ANALYTICS=false, chdirs into a temp dir, fakes HOME so the developer's real ~/.aider.conf.yml cannot leak in, and patches builtins.input plus webbrowser.open; tearDown (39-46) restores the environment. This is what isolates the three input sources so a CLI-versus-env precedence claim is testable at all.

main() forwards the parsed value verbatim into Coder.create as suggest_shell_commands=args.suggest_shell_commands (with detect_urls=args.detect_urls on line 1003). This closes the loop: whatever source wins at parse time is what appears as coder.suggest_shell_commands, so the precedence result is observable end to end rather than only at the argparse Namespace.

claims.claim: aider/args.py declares the T07 fixture as action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction with default=True, and get_parser builds a configargparse parser with auto_env_var_prefix="AIDER_"; the same option therefore has a CLI form, an AIDER_SUGGEST_SHELL_COMMANDS environment form, a .aider.conf.yml form, and a declared default of True -- the four ranks of the C-T07 lattice.

Because BooleanOptionalAction registers both --suggest-shell-commands and --no-suggest-shell-commands against the single dest suggest_shell_commands, an explicit CLI occurrence of either polarity can be expressed, and an explicit CLI occurrence is the highest-precedence input source: it must override an opposed AIDER_SUGGEST_SHELL_COMMANDS value or an opposed .aider.conf.yml value, in both directions (env=true + --no-... -> False; env=false + --... -> True).

Unrelated defaults are preserved under the override: --detect-urls (aider/args.py:842-847, default=True) and --cache-prompts (aider/args.py:232-237, default=False) are independent declarations that stay at their defaults while --suggest-shell-commands is forced to False by explicit CLI input. The contract is two-sided and a change that moves those options would violate it.

The repository's existing fixture at tests/basic/test_main.py:735-763 pins the observable to Coder.suggest_shell_commands via main(..., return_coder=True) for the default/disabled/enabled trio, but it exercises CLI-versus-default only and never opposes an env or config value against a CLI flag; T07 is the extension that adds that opposition, which is why it is a distinct fixture rather than a re-run of the trio.

Environment input is a real, boolean-valued, non-default source for this option family: tests/basic/test_main.py:421-462 shows .env values (AIDER_DARK_MODE=True, AIDER_SHOW_DIFFS=off/on) being loaded by main() and changing observed behavior, and setUp (22-37) isolates HOME and AIDER_* so the precedence can be attributed to a single source. Without a working env source there would be nothing for an explicit CLI flag to override.

The precedence verdict is observable end to end, not just in the argparse namespace: main() forwards args.suggest_shell_commands into Coder.create (aider/main.py:1000), so the winning source is readable as coder.suggest_shell_commands, matching how the existing fixture asserts it.

conclusion: Contract C-T07 holds for the new fixture: aider/args.py declares --suggest-shell-commands as a argparse.BooleanOptionalAction with default=True inside a configargparse parser whose auto_env_var_prefix="AIDER_" makes AIDER_SUGGEST_SHELL_COMMANDS and .aider.conf.yml real competing input sources, and BooleanOptionalAction gives an explicit CLI occurrence of either polarity a spelling that outranks them, while the independent declarations --detect-urls (True) and --cache-prompts (False) keep their declared defaults. The executable probe proves the declared shape and the explicit-CLI-polarity half of the contract with 18/18 executed checks passing and 0 failures; the env/config-versus-CLI half is asserted by construction and by the repository's existing env fixture, but its execution is dependency-gated and was skipped in this interpreter, so the honest status is partial, not pass.
